songs.name: I'm A Hog For You Baby

ai_show_review.summary: Blues‑driven early Dead set with fierce Jerry and Pigpen’s debut keys
ai_show_review.blurb: The four-song set showcases raw blues power, highlighted by Jerry Garcia's fire‑spitting lead on 'Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks)' that rolls straight into a searing 'Death Don't Have No Mercy'. Pigpen makes his first audible keyboard appearance, adding gritty organ to the same track. The band plays with high energy and tight cohesion despite the lo‑fi tape.
ai_show_review.review: The Jan 8 1966 Fillmore Acid Test captures the Grateful Dead in their formative blues‑heavy phase. From the opening riff of "I'm A King Bee" through a playful "I'm A Hog For You Baby," the group settles into a gritty groove that feels both spontaneous and tightly locked. Jerry's guitar is on fire, especially on the blistering "Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks)" which launches straight into a gut‑wrenching rendition of "Death Don't Have No Mercy." That moment also marks Pigpen’s first audible keyboard contribution, his organ tone cutting through the raw tape with historic significance. Bob Weir’s onstage antics—pole‑climbing jokes during the brief National Anthem jam—add classic early‑Dead humor, while Bill Kreutzmann lays down a solid, driving beat that holds the set together. Though the recordings are lo‑fi and show occasional dropouts, the energy is undeniable and the performance remains a vital snapshot of the band’s pre‑psychedelic evolution.

best_recording.reason: Most complete capture of the set; despite fair fidelity it preserves the full performance and historic ambience, making it the go‑to source for this early Acid Test show.

key_highlights: Fierce Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks) → Death Don't Have No Mercy sequence
Pigpen’s first audible keyboard/organ on Death Don't Have No Mercy

song_highlights: I'm A Hog For You Baby

band_performance.Jerry: Blazing, straight‑ahead blues lead; his tone on Caution and Death Don't Have No Mercy is raw and fierce.
band_performance.Bob: Adds classic early‑Dead humor with pole‑climbing antics during the National Anthem jam; solid rhythm guitar throughout.
band_performance.Pigpen: Makes a historic debut on keyboards, providing gritty organ texture that punctuates Death Don't Have No Mercy.
band_performance.Billy: Keeps a steady, driving beat that underpins the blues set and holds the band together despite tape limitations.
